problem_motivation.content: Precipitate distributions strongly govern alloy strength.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: The shape, particle size distribution (PSD) and spatial distribution of precipitates critically influence alloy strength.

prior_approach.content: Prior microscopy found spherical small precipitates.
prior_approach.evidence_span: Studies of similar alloys using transmission electron microscopy revealed spherical precipitates on the smallest length scales

prior_approach.content: The TIDC model broadens LSW distributions with an additional shape parameter.
prior_approach.evidence_span: For example, Ardell & Ozolins (2005 [2] ) developed the TIDC model of precipitation hardening, defining a PSD that incorporates a shape parameter in addition to a characteristic radius .

prior_approach.content: In situ scattering follows PSD evolution continuously in one heated specimen.
prior_approach.evidence_span: In situ X-ray or neutron scattering provides an alternative method for PSD study using sequential measurements on a single sample undergoing heat treatment.

prior_limitation.content: Assuming a PSD shape can bias scattering analysis.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: Unfortunately, a priori definition of a defined PSD shape for small-angle scattering (SAS) data analysis can give misleading results.

inspiration_source.content: Avoiding assumed PSD forms motivated the MaxEnt approach.
inspiration_source.evidence_span: The desire to avoid prior assumptions about the form of the PSD solution drove the development of MaxEnt approaches that seek the best explanation for the PSD given only the measured data and the shape of the precipitates.

causal_claim.content: Fine coherent ordered precipitates strengthen Ni superalloys.
causal_claim.evidence_span: The formation of fine, coherent, ordered, intermetallic precipitates in a face-centered cubic matrix strengthens Ni-based superalloys

mechanism_principle.content: LSW specifies a parameterized particle-radius distribution.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: LSW theory further specifies a functional form for the PSD characterized by a size parameter to yield a distribution of particle radii r

mechanism_principle.content: A flat prior makes new PSD peaks arise from measurement rather than assumed distribution shape.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: An uninformative flat prior for conveys no information about the form of the distribution; expecting a flat PSD at the outset means that new information (peaks) in comes only from the measurement.

mechanism_principle.content: Bayesian MaxEnt lets measurement uncertainty determine the regularization weight.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: Instead, the data and measurement error inherently dictate λ.

hypothesis_statement.content: Inverse transforms can infer PSDs without a preset form.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: Rather than beginning with a defined functional form for the PSD, inverse transform approaches seek an arbitrary size distribution that explains the observation

evidence_result.content: A new precipitate population appeared and coarsened during heat treatment.
evidence_result.evidence_span: During heat treatment, a new population of scatterers appears at high q and shifts to lower q with time, as expected from previous studies of precipitation behavior in this alloy system

evidence_result.content: Combined scattering reveals grain structure plus two precipitate-size populations.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The combined USAXS–SAXS data after heat treatment suggest the presence of three length scale regimes, namely a low- q power law region for the grain structure of the metal and two precipitate size distributions:

evidence_result.content: A new high-q precipitate population grows during heat treatment.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The high- q region shows growth of a new first PSD, consistent with precipitation hardening in Ni alloys.

evidence_result.content: PSD mode, inferred diameter, and superlattice growth follow similar temporal trajectories.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Plotting these three parameters on the same time axis demonstrates that all three follow similar trajectories.

constraint.content: The dilute-system assumption of LSW may fail in real alloys.
constraint.evidence_span: However, some assumptions of LSW theory, such as a dilute system of precipitates, may not apply to real systems.

constraint.content: Conventional inversion can fail when low-q background is nonflat or interparticle effects matter.
constraint.evidence_span: Conventional inverse transformation using equation (2) gives misleading results in the absence of flat at low q

constraint.content: Grain scattering, a second PSD, and structure-factor effects complicate MaxEnt inference.
constraint.evidence_span: The presence of the grain structure, second PSD and structure factor together makes implementation of MaxEnt difficult
